question:
A 24-year-old female presents to the emergency department with fever (101.2°F/38.4°C), cough
producing yellow sputum, and progressive dyspnea on exertion that developed after flu-like symptoms
one week ago. Her medical history includes hospitalization for pneumonia 4 months ago, bacteremia 6
weeks ago, and past IV heroin use (last use 3 years ago). Vital signs show BP 104/70 mmHg, pulse
115/min, and respirations 19/min. Physical exam reveals coarse breath sounds over the right lower
lung field, a soft 1/6 systolic flow murmur at the first right intercostal space, splenomegaly, and tender
wrists and fingers with limited range of motion that improves throughout the day. Which laboratory
finding would most likely be present in this patient? Answer Choices: (A) Elevated rheumatoid factor
(B) Neutropenia (C) Elevated ESR (D) Flow cytometry positive for CD11c and CD2 (E) Positive HIV
serology (F) Elevated procalcitonin levels (G) Elevated C-reactive protein (H) Positive antinuclear
antibodies (I) Thrombocytopenia (J) Positive blood cultures for MRSA
 A. Positive blood cultures for MRSA
B. Elevated procalcitonin levels
C. Positive HIV serology
D. Elevated C-reactive protein
E. Elevated rheumatoid factor
F. Flow cytometry positive for CD11c and CD2
G. Positive antinuclear antibodies
H. Thrombocytopenia
I. Elevated ESR
J. Neutropenia
